renderings.value: Denies a general assumption; 'it does not mean that', 'it's not the case'.

The ～わけではない grammar point is used to deny or correct a general assumption or statement without completely negating the situation. It often emphasizes one particular point that is not true, while acknowledging other possibilities.
Verb-casual + わけではない, い-Adjective + わけではない, な-Adjective + だわけではない, Noun + だわけではない
"It doesn't mean that/it's not the case that". (Near-duplicate of n2-164 - same construction, taught at both N2 and N3.)
Just because he's busy doesn't mean he has no friends.
It's not that this movie isn't interesting; it's just not my taste.
Just because she's sick doesn't mean she's in bed all day.
Just because he didn't go to college doesn't mean he's stupid.
